city.act.tickets.prompt: E — ask at the box office
city.bed.nap.1: I shut my eyes for a minute. When I opened them the window's shadow had crept onto the other wall.
city.bed.nap.2: I dozed to the ticking of the clock in the corridor. The dream was short and warm, like a sandwich.
city.bed.nap.3: A nurse looked in, tucked the blanket round me and left without a word.
city.bed.night.1: The sheets crackled with starch. The sea was murmuring outside, and then I heard nothing at all.
city.bed.night.2: I dreamt I was climbing an endless staircase to the sun and not getting tired at all.
city.bed.night.3: I woke to spoons ringing in glasses in the corridor: someone was bringing tea.
city.bed.private.1: This is someone's bed. The cover's been smoothed by a hand, there's a dent in the pillow. No.
city.bed.private.2: A stranger's bed smells of a stranger's soap. I just stood next to it.
city.bed.private.3: Someone else sleeps here. I have to find a place of my own.
city.do.aquarium.1: The guppies dart in a shoal, and the catfish lies on the bottom pretending to be a stone. He's good at it.
city.do.aquarium.2: One fish swam up to the glass and looked at me. I'm not sure which of us is in the tank.
city.do.aquarium.3: Bubbles rise steadily from the little castle on the bottom. Watch long enough and you start breathing in time.
city.do.aquarium.4: A sign on the tank: "Do not feed the fish. They are on a diet. Especially Boris." I couldn't find Boris.
city.do.arcade.1: "Sea Battle": I sank two ships out of five. The periscope smells of rubber and other people's foreheads.
city.do.arcade.2: Racing: on the third lap my car went into the ditch and stayed there. The machine beeped something sympathetic.
city.do.arcade.3: "Sniper": nine out of ten. The machine gave me a token for a free game, but the token rolled away somewhere.
city.do.arcade.4: I played "Goalkeeper" until three boys were queuing behind me. Gave way. They played worse.
city.do.barbell.1: I took off all the plates but two small ones. Lifted ten times. The plates weren't that small after all.
city.do.barbell.2: The coach straightened my back and said: "The strength is in your legs, not your face." I stopped grimacing.
city.do.barbell.3: The bar is cold and smells of iron. After the third set my arms hummed like wires.
city.do.barbell.4: Up, down, up. In the wall mirror, a boy with red ears and a very determined look.
city.do.basketball.1: Three out of ten. Every time the ball went thoughtfully round the rim, deciding whether to drop.
city.do.basketball.2: The net is torn, so you can hardly hear a basket. You have to take your own word for it.
city.do.basketball.3: A tall lad showed me how to put backspin on it. The ball obeyed him, and then me.
city.do.basketball.4: The ball thuds on the tarmac like a big heart. I kept going till the sun dropped behind the hoop.
city.do.billiards.1: Aimed for five minutes, struck, and the ball went round every cushion and quietly dropped in. I pretended I'd meant it.
city.do.billiards.2: A man in braces showed me how to chalk the cue and said: "It's not the ball that matters, it's the pause before the shot."
city.do.billiards.3: I'd have torn the cloth if they hadn't stopped me in time. They did. Let me play again, from a safe distance.
city.do.billiards.4: The balls click like chattering teeth. I potted two. Not bad, they say, for the first time in my life.
city.do.binoculars_post.1: Through the binoculars: the buoys, and nobody beyond them. Good. The lifeguard said: "If only it were always like this."
city.do.binoculars_post.2: I found a gull sitting on a buoy looking my way. We stared at each other for a long time.
city.do.binoculars_post.3: Far out a swimmer in a red cap goes steadily, unhurried, as if he knows where.
city.do.binoculars_post.4: The eyepieces are warm from other people's eyes. The sea is closer through them, but quieter, somehow.
city.do.binoculars_post.prompt: E — look through the lifeguard's binoculars
city.do.blackboard.1: I chalked "2 + 2 =" and paused. The chalk squeaked by itself, as if prompting.
city.do.blackboard.2: Left on the board from the last lesson: "On duty: Lebedev." I added: "and me".
city.do.blackboard.3: I drew a sun, rubbed it out, then drew it again, bigger. The cloth smells of chalk and wet wool.
city.do.blackboard.4: I wrote my name and looked at it a long time. On the board it looked like someone else's.
city.do.checkup.1: The doctor listened with a cold stethoscope and said: "Your heart works. Sometimes overtime."
city.do.checkup.2: "Say 'ah'." "Ahh." "Good. More sun, fewer sweets, and sleep at night."
city.do.checkup.3: The doctor tapped my knee with a little hammer and my leg jerked. "Reflexes fine. We'll check your thoughts another time."
city.do.checkup.4: They wrote "Practically healthy" on my card. I asked what "practically" means. The doctor smiled and didn't say.
city.do.chess.1: I lost to an old man in a beret. But he showed me the Sicilian defence and said I had "honest moves".
city.do.chess.2: Drew with a girl of about nine. She thought a long time over every move and swung her legs.
city.do.chess.3: I won! My opponent shook my hand and said he'd let me. Then he thought and said he hadn't.
city.do.chess.4: We both forgot whose move it was and started over. Then again. The game never really began, but it was nice.
city.do.chess.prompt: E — play a game of chess
city.do.choir.1: The choir sang without words, just voices, and the vaults overhead hummed like a vast seashell.
city.do.choir.2: The choir leader stopped them: "Altos, you're singing about the sun as if it were the bus timetable. Again!"
city.do.choir.3: An old man in the back row sang slightly off, but so happily that nobody corrected him.
city.do.choir.4: They went over the song about ten times, and on the tenth I caught myself quietly singing along.
city.do.choir.prompt: E — listen to the choir rehearsal
city.do.cinema.1: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. He waited forty years, and all that time the lighthouse waited for him. The whole hall cried at the end. Me too, a bit.
city.do.cinema.2: A comedy about a holidaymaker whose hat blew away. The hat flew round the whole town and came back. We laughed so hard the screen shook.
city.do.cinema.3: Before the film, the reel "The Sun Is Our Home". The film snapped at the best bit, and for a minute we all watched white light.
city.do.cinema.4: The film was old and silent, with a pianist playing along. By the end I felt it was me up there on the screen, walking down an empty street.
city.do.dance.1: I shuffled about to a waltz, counting one-two-three under my breath. On "three" I always trod on my own foot.
city.do.dance.2: An old couple turned so lightly the floor might have been water. I tried it: the floor turned out to be parquet.
city.do.dance.3: The dance teacher clapped: "Straighten your back, young man! You're not picking mushrooms!"
city.do.dance.4: The music stopped and I turned a little longer. Nobody laughed. That's how it's done here.
city.do.darkroom.1: In the red light the pier slowly surfaced on the white paper. As if someone were remembering it.
city.do.darkroom.2: Left it too long in the developer and the print went black. The club leader said: "Night photography. Conceptual."
city.do.darkroom.3: On someone else's film that we developed, there was me. From behind, on the promenade. I don't remember being photographed.
city.do.darkroom.4: It smells of vinegar and secrets. The prints dry on a line with clothes-pegs, like washing.
city.do.darkroom.prompt: E — develop prints in the darkroom
city.do.darts.1: First dart in the wall, second in the two, third dead in the bull. I stopped there so as not to spoil it.
city.do.darts.2: The board is full of holes like a night sky. I added three more stars.
city.do.darts.3: Someone behind me said: "Don't aim with your eye, aim with your elbow." I tried. Hit the door frame with my elbow.
city.do.darts.4: Forty-one points. Someone chalked my name on the board. Spelt wrong, but still nice.
city.do.easel.1: I painted the sea. It looks like the sea, if you really want it to. The studio leader said: "Bold."
city.do.easel.2: I mixed blue and yellow and got green. Mixed everything and got a puddle. That's a discovery too.
city.do.easel.3: I drew the sun in the corner like a little kid, with stick rays. Someone beside me sighed: "Like everyone does. And rightly so."
city.do.easel.4: I spent an hour on one cup. The cup came out crooked, but its shadow looks real.
city.do.exercise_bike.1: I rode three kilometres on the exercise bike and stayed where I was. Like in a dream.
city.do.exercise_bike.2: The counter's broken and always shows "12". I pedalled until twelve started to feel like a lot.
city.do.exercise_bike.3: The bike faces a window onto the sea. I imagined riding the promenade to the lighthouse, overtaking the bus.
city.do.exercise_bike.4: The pedals creak in waltz time. One-two-three, one-two-three. My legs got tired; the tune stayed.
city.do.eye_chart.1: E, F, P… T, O, Z… I read the bottom line by heart: it's the same in every clinic in the world.
city.do.eye_chart.2: I covered my left eye with the spoon. The right sees better, but the left seems to see something else.
city.do.eye_chart.3: "Twenty-twenty!" said the nurse. I was alarmed at first, then understood it was good.
city.do.eye_chart.4: The last line blurs and forms a word that isn't on the chart. I blinked, and everything was as it should be.
city.do.fortune.1: The mechanical fortune-teller nodded and gave me a card: "Soon you will be where you have already been."
city.do.fortune.2: The card: "Your sun is rising. Don't oversleep." In small print: "The machine accepts no responsibility."
city.do.fortune.3: The fortune-teller froze with her hand raised, thought, and gave me a blank card. Probably a good sign.
city.do.fortune.4: "The person you seek is seeking you too. Meet in the middle." The middle of what, it doesn't say.
city.do.fountain.1: The water's so cold my teeth ached. The jet squirts sideways, so I washed my face as well.
city.do.fountain.2: I drank and felt the water going down, as if someone had drawn a cool ruler through me.
city.do.fountain.3: The fountain tastes of iron and childhood. I don't know how I know what childhood tastes like.
city.do.fountain.4: A pigeon waited beside me while I drank. I stepped away and it didn't drink. Maybe it just wanted to stand there.
city.do.haircut.1: "How do you want it?" "However." "Short back and sides, then." Half an hour later I looked like a photo on a notice board.
city.do.haircut.2: The barber talked about fishing and never once looked at the scissors. It came out even. Nearly.
city.do.haircut.3: They sprayed me with cologne, and all evening I smell like someone's grandad at a party.
city.do.haircut.4: In the mirror facing the mirror I saw an endless corridor of me. In the furthest one I think I was smiling.
city.do.jukebox.1: I pressed B7 and A3 started playing. The machine knows best. A song about a gull who didn't come back.
city.do.jukebox.2: The record hisses like sea on shingle. A woman sings of a summer that "isn't over yet but is already remembered".
city.do.jukebox.3: I put on a foxtrot. Two old ladies by the window got up and went once round the floor, then sat down as if nothing had happened.
city.do.jukebox.4: The jukebox swallowed the coin and pondered. A minute later it played a march, loud and out of place.
city.do.lottery.1: I unrolled the ticket: "A postcard." No-lose means honest. A postcard of the lighthouse.
city.do.lottery.2: On the back of the winning ticket, handwritten: "And a little extra luck." They gave me no luck, just a postcard.
city.do.lottery.3: Three of us turned the ticket drum: me, the woman and the wind. Out came a postcard of the promenade.
city.do.lottery.4: "The top prize is a bicycle," the woman said. "Nobody's ever won it. Maybe it doesn't exist. Here's a postcard."
city.do.lottery.prompt: E — draw a no-lose lottery ticket
city.do.microphone.1: "One, two, testing." My voice flew round the hall and came back someone else's, grown up.
city.do.microphone.2: The mic howled, and the cleaner in the doorway shook her mop at me. I pretended it was intentional.
city.do.microphone.3: I said "Hello" to the empty hall. The hall didn't answer, but it seemed to be listening.
city.do.microphone.4: I wanted to sing but only remembered the chorus. Sang the chorus. The echo sang it again, better.
city.do.microphone.prompt: E — say something into the microphone
city.do.misc.1: I fiddled with it, prodded it, broke nothing. A success already.
city.do.misc.2: I didn't work out how it works, but I looked very serious.
city.do.misc.3: Someone had left a note on it: "Don't touch. Touched. Broken." I didn't touch it.
city.do.payphone.1: I dialled a number at random. A woman answered, said "Hello, hello", fell silent and said softly: "Is that you?" I hung up.
city.do.payphone.2: I rang the speaking clock. "The time is exactly…" and the voice faltered. Then went on brightly.
city.do.payphone.3: Long rings in the receiver, and between them a faraway murmur, like in a seashell.
city.do.payphone.4: The phone ate the coin and didn't connect. I thumped it, the way everyone does. It returned my coin and someone else's.
city.do.photo_booth.1: Four flashes. In the first I'm blinking, in the second serious, in the third smiling, in the fourth I'm not there.
city.do.photo_booth.2: The photographer ducked under the black cloth and said "watch the birdie". A real sparrow flew out from under the roof.
city.do.photo_booth.3: The prints were ready in ten minutes. I look more like myself in them than in a mirror. They're going in my diary.
city.do.photo_booth.4: The photographer stood me against a painted sea. The real one was right outside, but the painted one, he says, comes out better.
city.do.piano.1: I played "Chopsticks" with one finger. Behind a door someone joined in on a violin, in a different key.
city.do.piano.2: One key sticks and sounds like a cough. I played the whole tune so as to avoid it.
city.do.piano.3: I pressed three white keys in a row and got something like a sunrise. Couldn't do it again.
city.do.piano.4: The music on the stand says "play as if no one is listening". I did. And no one was.
city.do.pool.1: I swam four lengths of crawl and two of doggy paddle. The lifeguard whistled, approvingly I think.
city.do.pool.2: Underwater everything is green and echoing. I lay on the bottom and watched the light dance over the tiles in a net.
city.do.pool.3: It smells of chlorine and wet towels. I got out and my body felt heavy and happy.
city.do.pool.4: A granny in a flowery cap swam beside me and lapped me twice. She said she'd been swimming like that for fifty years.
city.do.potters_wheel.1: The clay spun and wriggled out of my hands like a live fish. It ended up an ashtray. I'd wanted a vase.
city.do.potters_wheel.2: The potter laid her hands over mine and the walls rose by themselves. "Like that. Don't press. Persuade."
city.do.potters_wheel.3: Clay up to my elbows. The little bowl is lopsided, but it's mine. They promised to fire it by Thursday.
city.do.potters_wheel.4: The wheel hums like a bumblebee, and to that hum I stopped thinking entirely. Very useful.
city.do.potters_wheel.prompt: E — sit at the potter's wheel
city.do.pump_room.1: I filled a bottle at the tap. The water smells of iron and a bit of egg. "Good for you," said a guest in a sun hat.
city.do.pump_room.2: In the pump room everyone sips from the spouts of china mugs and looks out of the window as if at a screen.
city.do.pump_room.3: A sign by the spring: "Temperature 12°. High mineral content. Drink slowly, think of good things."
city.do.pump_room.4: The water runs warm from the tap, as if it passed something hot underground. The sun, probably.
city.do.pump_room.prompt: E — fill a bottle with mineral water
city.do.punching_bag.1: The bag swung and came back, like a grudge. I hit it until it was just a bag.
city.do.punching_bag.2: An old coach showed me a one-two and said: "Punch as if you're knocking on a door you really need."
city.do.punching_bag.3: The gloves are too big and smell of other people's victories. The bag is old leather, all patches.
city.do.punching_bag.4: After ten minutes I was puffing like a steam engine, and inside it went quiet and empty, like a gym in the evening.
city.do.record_player.1: I lowered the needle. Crackle first, then a violin, then crackle again, as if the music were coming through rain.
city.do.record_player.2: On the sleeve, an orchestra on a beach, all in tailcoats and barefoot.
city.do.record_player.3: The record stuck on one phrase: "…and the sun, and the sun, and the sun…" I didn't fix it.
city.do.record_player.4: A fairy-tale record. The narrator's voice is so kind I listened to the whole of "The Runaway Bun", though I know how it ends.
city.do.ring_toss.1: One ring landed on a bottle and slid straight off. The woman said: "I'll count it, you tried."
city.do.ring_toss.2: The rings are as light as pancakes and fly where they like. One went into the ice cream kiosk next door.
city.do.ring_toss.3: Three out of three! The prize was a paper flower. I tucked it in my breast pocket. It looks good there.
city.do.ring_toss.4: The boy next to me scored every time and dutifully gave the prizes to his little sister. I watched instead of throwing.
city.do.scales.1: The nurse slid the weight along and wrote down a number. "You're growing," she said. I didn't know I was.
city.do.scales.2: The scales showed the same as yesterday, though I wasn't here yesterday. The nurse wasn't surprised.
city.do.scales.3: I took my trainers off to make it fairer. Three hundred grams lighter, and one small worry less.
city.do.scales.4: Height and weight went into a card in beautiful handwriting. The card, it turned out, already had my name on it.
city.do.school_desk.1: Geography. The teacher pointed on the map to where we live, and there was only blue paint there.
city.do.school_desk.2: Literature: poems about autumn. The boy by the window read so well that it clouded over outside for a minute.
city.do.school_desk.3: Carved on the desk: "Whoever reads this is great." I read it. Astronomy, topic: "Our Sun". I listened without breathing.
city.do.school_desk.4: Nobody asked who I was. They gave me a squared exercise book and said: "Take notes, you'll be asked later."
city.do.school_desk.prompt: E — sit in on a lesson
city.do.sewing_machine.1: The machine chirred like a grasshopper. The seam went zigzag though I wanted straight. Zigzag is a style too.
city.do.sewing_machine.2: I sewed a sun-shaped patch on my jacket. The women in the circle said that's what's in this season.
city.do.sewing_machine.3: The thread snapped, the needle broke, and the machine, an old Seagull older than my mum, carried on as if nothing had happened.
city.do.sewing_machine.4: I learnt to thread a needle. On the twelfth try it worked, and I felt like a surgeon.
city.do.shooting_gallery.1: I knocked down the duck, the windmill and the bear. The bear played a tune as it fell. The man said it hadn't done that in ages.
city.do.shooting_gallery.2: The rifle pulls left. I aimed further right, and it took offence and started pulling right.
city.do.shooting_gallery.3: Five shots, no hits. But now I know exactly where their light bulb hangs.
city.do.shooting_gallery.4: I hit the little sun on the backdrop. It didn't fall, just swayed. The man went pale for some reason.
city.do.slide_projector.1: A filmstrip, "The Journey of a Droplet". It evaporated, became a cloud, fell as rain and went back to the sea. Happy ending.
city.do.slide_projector.2: A frame jammed and a surprised-looking owl hung on the wall for ages. Everyone laughed; the owl went on being surprised.
city.do.slide_projector.3: Slides from someone's trip north: a geyser, snow, tents, people in jumpers squinting at the sun.
city.do.slide_projector.4: Click, a new frame. Click, another. The projector hums warmly like a cat and smells of heated dust.
city.do.stage.1: They were rehearsing a play about fishermen. An actor in a pea coat forgot his lines, and the prompter whispered them to the whole hall.
city.do.stage.2: A conjurer pulled a pigeon from his hat, then another, then another. They settled on the chandelier and stayed.
city.do.stage.3: A children's troupe danced the sailors' hornpipe. The smallest sailor was always a beat behind and the best of them all.
city.do.stage.4: The stage is empty, one spotlight on. Somehow watching an empty stage is as interesting as a full one.
city.do.strongman.1: The needle crawled up to "Schoolboy". Fair enough. I am one.
city.do.strongman.2: I hit it so hard the bell at the top rang. Everyone turned. I turned too, to see who'd done it.
city.do.strongman.3: Missed. The mallet slipped, and the tester showed "Dreamer". There's no such mark on it, actually.
city.do.strongman.4: "Hero"! Well, nearly: "Nearly Hero". My palm stings, but the pride stings more.
city.do.table_football.1: I spun the rods so hard the goalie did a somersault. I let the goal in anyway.
city.do.table_football.2: One player has a chipped nose and always misses. I named him Senya and cheered for him.
city.do.table_football.3: Five–three! The boys round the table clapped as if it were a World Cup final.
city.do.table_football.4: The ball got stuck in a corner and the two of us shook the table for a minute. Best part of the game.
city.do.table_tennis.1: We played to eleven. The ball went under the radiator twice, and both times the cleaner fished it out with her mop.
city.do.table_tennis.2: My opponent served with so much spin the ball seemed to go back to him on its own. Lost, but learnt the stance.
city.do.table_tennis.3: Tock-tock-tock. In five minutes I forgot everything but the white ball. Better than sleep.
city.do.table_tennis.4: The net sagged, the bat was sticky and the ball had a dent. 11–9 to me. Not fair, but nice.
city.do.telescope.1: The coin clinked and the shutter opened. I saw a barge, on the barge a dog, and the dog looking very important.
city.do.telescope.2: I pointed the telescope at the horizon. Where the sea ends something glints: a wave or a window.
city.do.telescope.3: I found our lighthouse through it, then my own footprints on the sand, then my time ran out.
city.do.telescope.4: I looked north at the mountains. On one slope something is steaming, thin as a kettle in a faraway kitchen.
city.do.track.1: I ran on the roof, with the whole town and the whole sea below. It felt as if with a big enough run-up I could take off.
city.do.track.2: Three laps. At every bend the wind changed: at my back, in my face, from the side smelling of fried fish.
city.do.track.3: Painted on the track: starts, finishes and, for some reason, a little sun. I finished on the sun.
city.do.track.4: An old resident jogged beside me in tracksuit bottoms and said he'd run here since the building went up. He wasn't even out of breath.
city.do.track.prompt: E — run a lap of the roof track
city.do.tv.1: A wildlife programme was on. A pelican swallowed a fish and looked into the camera as if waiting for applause.
city.do.tv.2: The weather: "Sunny tomorrow. Sunny the day after. Beyond that we haven't looked yet."
city.do.tv.3: The set showed only snow, and the guests watched it anyway, swaying their heads as if it were the sea.
city.do.tv.4: A request concert was on. Someone from Lyudmilovsk asked for a song "for the one who'll come back". It was a song about summer.
city.do.wall_bars.1: I climbed right up to the ceiling. From there you can see a volleyball on top of the cupboard, lost about five years ago.
city.do.wall_bars.2: I hung and raised my legs in an L. My stomach protested, but my head cleared.
city.do.wall_bars.3: The rungs are smooth as river pebbles: so many hands have held them.
city.do.wall_bars.4: I hung upside down and the world turned over. It's not bad that way either, it turns out.
city.do.wall_bars.prompt: E — hang on the wall bars
city.do.watch.1: I watched until I forgot I was watching. That only happens with the sea and fire.
city.do.watch.2: Nothing special happened, and that was good.
city.do.watch.3: Time went past me like a tram past an empty stop.
city.do.workbench.1: I planed a block of wood. The shavings curled like the hair of the girl on a postcard. Smells of pine and summer.
city.do.workbench.2: Got the nail in on the third try. The first two went into my thumb. The shop teacher said: "Happens. You'll remember now."
city.do.workbench.3: I made a nesting box. Crooked, but they say birds prefer them that way: cosier.
city.do.workbench.4: Carved into the bench: "Vitya was here, 1979." I thought about it and carved nothing.
city.door.any.1: Locked. Behind the door a tap is dripping.
city.door.any.2: The door won't give. Not today, probably.
city.door.roof.1: "Roof access. No unauthorised persons." The caretaker probably has the key.
city.door.roof.2: Wind and sunlight seep from under the door. Up there you must see the whole sea.
city.door.staff.1: "Staff only." Behind the door someone is laughing and clinking cups.
city.door.staff.2: A sign: "Knock before entering." I knocked. Nobody answered.
city.look.catalogue.1: I pulled out the catalogue drawer for S. Cards: "Steamers", "Sand", "Seabirds", "Sea, see also Memory".
city.look.catalogue.2: A handwritten card: "The book everyone's looking for. Shelf mark: none. Location: with whoever is reading it."
city.look.catalogue.3: In the drawer for S there are more cards on the sun than on anything else. The drawer won't shut properly.
city.look.catalogue.4: A card marked "On loan" has been in the catalogue for twenty years. To whom isn't written.
city.look.catalogue.5: The drawers smell of glue and wood. Run a finger along the cards and they rustle like dry grass in the northern meadows.
city.look.cinema.1: A poster: The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. Drama. A grey fisherman and a huge yellow beam that looks right at you.
city.look.cinema.2: "Children's show: The Hedgehog's Cable Car Adventure. Sundays at 11:00. Under sixes with a parent or a hedgehog."
city.look.cinema.3: The comedy "Unpaid Leave": on the poster a holidaymaker chases his flying hat across the whole town.
city.look.cinema.4: "Before the film, a science reel: 'The Sun Is Our Home'." Someone added underneath: "And we're the guests."
city.look.cinema.5: The week's programme: the same film every day. Under the table: "By popular demand."
city.look.club.1: "Amateur photography circle. Thursday, 18:00. Bring film and a good mood. Film is a must."
city.look.club.2: "Dances for the over… for anyone. Saturday, 19:00. Waltz, foxtrot, slow ones on request."
city.look.club.3: "Chess tournament. The winner gets a cup, the losers get tea. The tea's better, we've checked."
city.look.club.4: "The choir needs basses. No tenors, please: our tenors already sing for everyone."
city.look.club.5: "Lecture: 'Why do we love the sun?' Free entry. Questions from the floor welcome; answers not guaranteed."
city.look.exhibit.1: A plaque: "Anchor of the schooner Lyudmila, 18—. Found by divers in 19—. The schooner itself has never been found."
city.look.exhibit.2: "Model of the first cable car cabin, scale 1:10." Inside sits a tiny passenger with a newspaper.
city.look.exhibit.3: A case of amber. In one piece a mosquito is frozen, looking as if it's about to say something.
city.look.exhibit.4: "Sundial from the old Sun Square. The shadow tells the time to the nearest quarter hour, and mood."
city.look.exhibit.5: Trophies of the Surf sports society. The smallest is engraved: "For the will to win. Nearly won."
city.look.health.1: A poster: "Wash your hands before meals!" The drawn boy washes them with such joy you'd think it was the sea.
city.look.health.2: "Sunbathing: no more than 20 minutes. The sun isn't going anywhere, but you'll burn."
city.look.health.3: "A holidaymaker's day": rise, exercises, breakfast, sea, lunch, quiet hour, sea, supper, sea, sleep.
city.look.health.4: A chart: "How to breathe sea air properly." In on a count of four, out on the count of a wave.
city.look.health.5: "Vaccinations on Wednesdays. Crying is permitted any day."
city.look.lost.1: "Found: horn-rimmed glasses. Good eyesight. Ask at the cloakroom."
city.look.lost.2: "Lost: Barsik the cat, ginger, answers to a rustling bag. Finder gets eternal gratitude and pies."
city.look.lost.3: "Whoever took my striped deckchair from the beach, please bring it back: it remembers my back."
city.look.lost.4: "Found: a key on a blue ribbon. What it opens is unknown. Possibly something important."
city.look.lost.5: "Lost: the feeling that everything is still ahead. If found, keep it, you need it more." Unsigned.
city.look.misc.1: Notices pasted one over another like layers of paint. The bottom one has gone the colour of tea.
city.look.misc.2: "Whoever found a blue umbrella: it means a lot to me. Ask for Tamara Ilyinichna."
city.look.misc.3: The drawing pins are all colours, and one is shaped like a little sun. Nobody seems to touch that one.
city.look.misc.4: I read everything, down to "Notices are kept for 10 days." This one's been up about ten years.
city.look.painting.1: A painting, "Morning on the Pier": fishermen, gulls, mist. In the corner a boy in a hood is looking not at the sea but straight at me.
city.look.painting.2: A still life: a watermelon, a knife, tea in a glass holder. The tea is painted so you can see it going cold.
city.look.painting.3: A huge panel: people reach their hands towards the sun, and the sun reaches back. The fingers almost touch.
city.look.painting.4: A watercolour, "The Northern Meadows". The grass is a single brushstroke, and it seems to sway in the wind right now.
city.look.painting.5: A portrait of a woman in blue. The label: "Unknown artist. Unknown sitter. Very familiar."
city.look.prices.1: "Apples 5 rub., corn 14, seeds 9. The seller's smile free, but not always in stock."
city.look.prices.2: In chalk on a board: "Adyghe cheese. Fresh. Yesterday's is fresh too, just less so."
city.look.prices.3: "Check scales. Weigh your purchase!" Beside it, old scales with weights; one weight has a chipped edge.
city.look.prices.4: "Fish bought from the public from 6 to 9 a.m. Fish with stories, any time."
city.look.prices.5: Market rules: "Trading until 18:00. After 18:00, conversation only."
city.look.rules.1: "Library rules. 1: Keep quiet. 2: Especially in the capsules. 3: Whispering counts as quiet."
city.look.rules.2: "Books are lent for 14 days. Poetry for as long as you need."
city.look.rules.3: "Don't fold the corners of pages. That's what bookmarks, memory and the librarian are for."
city.look.rules.4: "A library card is issued on showing a passport or an honest face."
city.look.rules.5: "Taking books out of the reading room is forbidden. Taking thoughts out is encouraged."
city.look.store.1: Store directory: "Ground floor: grocery, confectionery, haberdashery, drinks. First floor: books, sports, garden, souvenirs. Second floor: none."
city.look.store.2: "Dear customers! First choose, then pay at the till, then collect. The order matters, as in life."
city.look.store.3: "The complaints and suggestions book is kept by the manager." Below, in small print: "There are more suggestions."
city.look.store.4: "Fresh bread delivered at 9:00 and 16:00. Pies when you're lucky."
city.look.store.5: A poster, "Summer Is Holiday Time!": a family with a rubber ring and a ball. The dad is very tanned and the mum very happy.
city.look.timetable.1: "Bus No. 3: Promenade, School, Sanatorium. Every 20 minutes, or however it works out."
city.look.timetable.2: Cable car times: first cabin 6:00, last 23:40. Added underneath: "The last one is for those in no hurry to get home."
city.look.timetable.3: A week's tide table. Someone crossed out Thursday and wrote: "On Thursdays the sea rests."
city.look.timetable.4: The local train "to the Northern Meadows" leaves on Saturdays at 7:15. A dry blade of grass is pinned beside it.
city.look.timetable.5: Opening hours for the bathhouse, the post office and the lighthouse. For the lighthouse: "Always. Especially at night."
city.look.view.1: The sea is striped today: turquoise by the shore, blue further out, nearly silver at the horizon.
city.look.view.2: Down below a tiny bus crawls along the promenade, and above it a cable car cabin, as if they were racing.
city.look.view.3: To the north, beyond the roofs, the mountains go blue, and on one summit lies a patch of snow. In summer. Strange and beautiful.
city.look.view.4: West of town the sand rolls away in waves to the edge of the world. Somehow I can't look that way for long.
city.look.view.5: The sun lies on the water in a path straight to me. Wherever I stand, the path turns to follow.
city.look.wallpaper.1: The school wall newspaper: class 7B on cleaning the beach and finding a message in a bottle. The note is in a foreign language.
city.look.wallpaper.2: "Our Top Pupils": the photos smile; one boy has his eyes shut. Underneath: "Blinked at the crucial moment."
city.look.wallpaper.3: A poem by a girl in 5A: "The sun sits down in the sea / as if in a warm bath. / Tomorrow it'll wake up early / all rosy and laughing."
city.look.wallpaper.4: A cartoon: the physics teacher as a pendulum. Caption: "Wavers, but holds on." They say the teacher liked it.
city.look.wallpaper.5: From the pupils' council: "Waste paper drive. The heaviest class gets a cake. Don't hand in encyclopaedias, it's a shame."

city.read.art.1: An album by a marine painter. He painted the same pier a hundred times and never got it the same twice.
city.read.art.2: "How to Paint Light." First tip: you can't paint light, you can only leave room for it on the paper.
city.read.art.3: A mosaic exhibition catalogue. In one, a woman holds the sun the way you'd hold a hot frying pan: carefully, a little afraid.
city.read.art.4: A book about this very library: the capsules, it turns out, were meant as "rooms to be alone in without being lonely".
city.read.art.5: Children's drawings published as a book. Under one: "This is my dad at work. Work is where he glows."
city.read.birds.1: "Birds of the Coast: a Field Guide." The laughing gull isn't laughing at you, says a footnote. That's just her voice.
city.read.birds.2: Starlings, the author writes, can imitate a creaking gate, a ringing telephone and a woman calling her cat in.
city.read.birds.3: Chapter: "How to attract a rare bird." A feeder, patience, and not one sudden movement. "Patience" is underlined twice.
city.read.birds.4: On a plate, a jay at life size. The wing feather is so blue I want to touch it to see if it's wet.
city.read.birds.5: The last page: "Birds remember the way to the sun better than we do. If you get lost, watch where they fly in autumn."
city.read.chess.1: A book of studies. White to play and win, if they think of sacrificing the queen. I didn't.
city.read.chess.2: Club championship games, written out by hand. One move is marked "?!" and beside it: "but beautiful".
city.read.chess.3: "Chess for Beginners": the knight moves in an L because, the author explains, it's more fun that way.
city.read.chess.4: An article on the Sicilian defence. I read it twice and understood only that you can defend with gusto too.
city.read.chess.5: A problem on the last page: "Mate in two. Solution in the next issue." The next issue isn't on the shelf.
city.read.cooking.1: A cookbook worn soft with use. On the pie page, a grease stain shaped like Africa.
city.read.cooking.2: A recipe for Lyudmilovsk fish soup: fish, potatoes, onion and "a pinch of fireside talk". Without the last one, it says, it won't work.
city.read.cooking.3: Recipe cards in many handwritings. One says "Granny Zoya's honey cake. Show no one." It's been shown to everyone.
city.read.cooking.4: Japanese cooking for beginners: wash the rice "until the water is as clear as morning". Mornings must be special there.
city.read.cooking.5: A chapter called "Sunshine Jam": apricots, sugar and a south-facing windowsill. Not a word on how to eat it after.
city.read.engineering.1: "Cable Cars: Design and Operation." The tensioning diagram looks like a spider's drawing after a drafting course.
city.read.engineering.2: Plans for a house on stilts. In the margin the architect wrote: "Let the wind walk under the house, and children run there."
city.read.engineering.3: A young engineers' magazine: how to build a radio in a matchbox. I stared at the diagram so long I heard the sea.
city.read.engineering.4: A handbook of lighthouses: a Fresnel lens gathers light the way cupped hands gather water from a stream.
city.read.engineering.5: A textbook on computing machines with a punch card for a bookmark. The holes look like a constellation.
city.read.garden.1: "A Garden in the Sea Wind": what to plant so it won't blow away. The author's answer: "Patience. And sea buckthorn."
city.read.garden.2: A gardener's calendar. For April: "Sow dill, talk to the apple tree." The second is underlined.
city.read.garden.3: A schoolboy's herbarium in a folder. Under a pressed daisy: "Found by the sea. Smelt of sunshine."
city.read.garden.4: How to grow tomatoes on a ninth-floor balcony. The main thing, the author writes, is not to look down and to praise the seedlings often.
city.read.garden.5: A sunflower, the note says, turns its head after the sun only while it's young. Later it faces east and waits.
city.read.kids.1: A pop-up book about a hedgehog who wanted to see the sea. On the last page the sea unfolds right into your hands. I jumped.
city.read.kids.2: "Tales of the Lighthouse." In one the lighthouse falls in love with a star, in another with a steamer. The star never knew.
city.read.kids.3: A picture alphabet: "A for anchor, B for buoy, C for cable car…" Under "Me" there's a boy who looks a lot like me.
city.read.kids.4: A colouring book where someone coloured the sun with felt tip right through the paper: three layers, yellow, orange, yellow again.
city.read.kids.5: A "Why?" encyclopaedia. Why is the sky blue, why is the sea salty, why do we sleep. The last one has no answer, just "sleep".
city.read.local.1: "Lyudmilovsk: a Short Guide." The town, it says, was founded "in time immemorial, roughly on a Thursday".
city.read.local.2: A photo album: the promenade without palms, the square without a fountain, the cable car without cabins. The people in the photos are the ones walking about today.
city.read.local.3: A local history collection: Sun Square once had a great sundial. They say it ran fast whenever the town had a holiday.
city.read.local.4: A list of streets and their old names. One street used to be called "The Street We Walked Home Along". It's written just like that.
city.read.local.5: A pamphlet about the Mires west of town: "Visits are not advised. Reasons are not given, but you will feel them."
city.read.medicine.1: "The Home Doctor." For a cold, tea with raspberry; for melancholy, a walk by the sea. The second has a tick beside it.
city.read.medicine.2: A poster-pamphlet: "The sun is a friend, but even friends have bad days. Wear a sun hat."
city.read.medicine.3: An anatomy atlas. The heart is drawn in such detail it feels rude to look, like peeping.
city.read.medicine.4: A book on sanatorium cures: "Sea air, mineral water and no hurry." The last, it says, is the one least often prescribed.
city.read.medicine.5: A nurse's handbook. In round handwriting in the margin: "The patient in 12 asked again what the sun was like today. I said: good."
city.read.misc.1: I leafed through at random. In the margin someone had neatly underlined one word: "always".
city.read.misc.2: The book fell open by itself at page forty: people must often open it there.
city.read.misc.3: Between the pages: a pressed maple leaf and a tram ticket with no date.
city.read.misc.4: I read half a chapter and realised I'd read it before. I just don't remember where.
city.read.music.1: A teach-yourself guitar book, three chords. On page four someone gave up and drew a cat in the margin.
city.read.music.2: Sheet music for the waltz "Mist Over the Sea". I can't read music, but you can tell by the look of it: slow and a little guilty.
city.read.music.3: A biography of a conductor who once stopped the orchestra so everyone could hear a thrush singing outside.
city.read.music.4: A record catalogue from the Surf label. Next to the song "Sunbeam Bunny" someone has put five exclamation marks.
city.read.music.5: A solfège textbook. "Do" is home, "sol" is the sun, and "ti" is anyone's guess. The author doesn't know either.
city.read.poetry.1: A thin book by a local poet. "The sea writes on the sand / and wipes it all away, / as if it can't quite trust / the draft of its own grey."
city.read.poetry.2: Poems about the cable car: the cabins are "glass nuts on a string". Lovely, though it's unclear who'd crack them.
city.read.poetry.3: An inscription in ink on the flyleaf: "For Lida, so she won't miss the south. Though how much further south can you get." An illegible signature.
city.read.poetry.4: A haiku in translation: "The old pier. / The gull says nothing, / the wave finishes." The translator must have stood on a pier a long time.
city.read.poetry.5: "I saw the sun from within: / it's like a house where someone waits." Then the page is stained with tea, and I never found out who.
city.read.science.1: "Physics for the Curious." If the Earth stopped, the author writes, we'd all fly east. Politely, without panic.
city.read.science.2: A kitchen experiment: a glass of water, a postcard, turn it over. The water stays in. Pencilled beside it: "It doesn't. Tested. Mum."
city.read.science.3: An old science magazine: an article on how machines will learn to think. The last paragraph has been neatly cut out with scissors.
city.read.science.4: A chapter on light: a ray from the Sun takes eight minutes. So I always see the sun as it was eight minutes ago. A bit sad.
city.read.science.5: The periodic table across two pages. Someone pencilled in a hundred-and-nineteenth box and labelled it "lyudmilium".
city.read.sea.1: "Sailing Directions for Lyudmilovsk Bay." Depths in fathoms, shoals marked with crosses, and one with a question mark.
city.read.sea.2: The handbook says the tide here comes not by the timetable but "when it sees fit". Tables attached, just in case.
city.read.sea.3: A book of sea knots. I learnt the figure-eight and tied my shoelace with it at once. Took five minutes to undo.
city.read.sea.4: An old lighthouse keeper's memoir: in forty years he never saw the sea repeat itself. Not one wave the same.
city.read.sea.5: On the current chart the bay looks like a palm and the currents like the lines on it. The long one runs right through the pier.
city.read.sun.1: "The Sun is an ordinary star," the textbook begins. Then it spends twenty pages proving it's nothing of the sort.
city.read.sun.2: A star atlas. A pencil note by the constellation Cygnus: "You can see us from here. Probably."
city.read.sun.3: A pamphlet, "Solar Energy Serving the Town". On the cover, a vast sphere of mirrors round the Sun. Caption: "A project. Someday."
city.read.sun.4: A chapter on sunspots. People have been counting them for centuries, as if someone were counting the sun like loose change.
city.read.sun.5: An old calendar of sunrises and sunsets. Next to the longest day someone drew a little bonfire and wrote: "Don't sleep".
city.read.travel.1: "Shores" magazine: photos of every lighthouse on the coast. Ours is the double spread, and the caption, oddly, says "You are here".
city.read.travel.2: A guide to the north: volcanoes, fumaroles, snowfields and meadows where "the grass is knee-high and the sky lower than usual".
city.read.travel.3: A timetable of ferries that no longer sail. Someone ringed one crossing, "Lyudmilovsk to Far Shore, 06:40", and wrote: "Waiting".
city.read.travel.4: A traveller's diary: "Day three. Went nowhere. Sat on the promenade. Best day of the trip."
city.read.travel.5: An atlas with a sheet glued in: a map of places on no other map. The furthest is labelled simply "later".

city.take.any.1: Nothing left here. Someone got here first.
city.take.any.2: Empty. Only a dusty rectangle where something used to lie.
city.take.daily_paper.1: I took a paper. On the front page, a fisherman with a flounder the size of a saucepan lid.
city.take.daily_paper.2: Today's issue. Forecast: clear, wind off the sea, music in the park possible in the evening.
city.take.daily_paper.3: The paper's still warm, as if it had just been printed behind the wall.
city.take.postcard.1: I took a postcard of the promenade. The sky on it is bluer than it ever really is.
city.take.postcard.2: A "Greetings from Lyudmilovsk!" card. Nobody to send it to, but I'll keep it.
city.take.postcard.3: On the back someone had pencilled "Dear…" and never finished.
city.talk.butcher.1: The butcher hones his knife and nods to me like an old friend. There's nothing for me to buy from him.
city.talk.butcher.2: "Out of mince, come early tomorrow. Scraps for the cats are free."
city.talk.butcher.3: Above the counter, a chart of beef cuts. The cow on it looks very calm.
city.talk.butcher.4: "What a sun today, eh? Even the meat looks rosier," said the butcher, surprised at himself.
city.talk.cashier.1: "First the department, they write you a slip, then me, then back to the department. Clear?" "Clear."
city.talk.cashier.2: The cashier clacks the till so fast she seems to be playing a polka on it.
city.talk.cashier.3: "No small change? What if you look?" I looked. Found a button.
city.talk.cashier.4: By the till there's a saucer for change with one sweet in it. Change too, apparently.
city.talk.cloakroom.1: "Don't lose your token," said the attendant, though I had nothing to hand in.
city.talk.cloakroom.2: The hangers sway and chime softly, like wind chimes.
city.talk.cloakroom.3: "In summer we get only umbrellas, and one hat. The hat's been here since the spring before last."
city.talk.cloakroom.4: The attendant is knitting something long and striped. A scarf, she says. Three years now, she says.
city.talk.closed.1: Nobody. A note on the glass: "Gone to the depot. Back at 15:00." No date.
city.talk.closed.2: The counter's bare: an abacus and a glass of pencils. I tapped on the glass. Silence.
city.talk.closed.3: "Stocktaking." The sign hangs crooked, as if it went up in a hurry long ago.
city.talk.closed.4: Looks like they only sell to the neighbours, and the neighbours are all at home.
city.talk.counter.1: "Can I help you, young man?" "Just looking." "Look all you like."
city.talk.counter.2: Behind the counter someone is writing in a fat ledger and raises a finger: "One moment."
city.talk.counter.3: "Our break's from one to two, but for you, all right."
city.talk.counter.4: They smiled at me as if I came in every day. Maybe I really do.
city.talk.fishmonger.1: "The flounder's this morning's, the herring's yesterday's, and the gobies — don't ask."
city.talk.fishmonger.2: The fishwife weighs fish in her hand more exactly than the scales. The scales don't argue.
city.talk.fishmonger.3: "Catch something yourself, bring it here, I'll buy it," she said with a wink.
city.talk.fishmonger.4: One fish with a golden flank lies on the ice. "Not for sale," they say. "It's for luck."
city.talk.office.1: "Pass? No pass, no entry. Sit on the sofa and think about it."
city.talk.office.2: The porter doesn't look up from his crossword. "Heavenly body, three letters?" "Sun." "Fits."
city.talk.office.3: "Visitors from nine. And whom are you here to see?" "I… nobody yet."
city.talk.office.4: A bell on the desk and a sign: "Ring once." I rang once. That was enough.
city.talk.reception.1: "Are you a guest? No? Then at least have some water, ours is medicinal."
city.talk.reception.2: A bell on the desk and a booking book for treatments. Next to every name, a little drawn sun.
city.talk.reception.3: "Breakfast from eight, dinner till seven, the sea round the clock," the receptionist rattled off.
city.talk.reception.4: "No rooms. But if you really need one, in 204 only one floorboard creaks."
city.talk.rentals.1: "Boats till sunset, deckchairs till six, umbrellas till the first rain."
city.talk.rentals.2: "Deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. Got one of those?"
city.talk.rentals.3: Oars stand along the wall, numbered in paint. Number seven is missing: it went to sea last July.
city.talk.rentals.4: "The bikes are being repaired," sighed the man. "All of them. At once. A mystery."
city.talk.repair.1: The repairman doesn't look up from the watch. "Leave it, a week." "I've nothing to leave." "Even better."
city.talk.repair.2: On the shelf an iron, a transistor radio and a toy railway wait for their owners. The tag says "Urgent. 1987".
city.talk.repair.3: "You can fix anything but the weather and a mood," the repairman said, and fixed my shoelace.
city.talk.repair.4: It smells of rosin and machine oil. Somewhere in a corner twenty clocks tick at once, all out of step.
city.talk.tickets.1: "Tickets are thirty roubles, pay in the hall. Sit anywhere, it's not busy."
city.talk.tickets.2: "Today it's The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. They say everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist."
city.talk.tickets.3: The cashier checks the poster against the wall clock, though the clock has stopped.
city.talk.tickets.4: "Under sixteens aren't allowed at the late show. How old are you? Never mind, don't answer."
quest.checkup.desc: At the clinic they looked at me as if I'd been due for a check-up for ages. Well, if they've been waiting.
quest.checkup.doctor.log: Only the doctor left. He sees patients on weekdays until five.
quest.checkup.done: "Practically healthy," they wrote on my card. The nurse gave me a boiled sweet as if I were little. I didn't refuse.
quest.checkup.nurse.log: The nurse told me to step on the scales and read the eye chart. Then the doctor.
quest.checkup.title: Practically healthy
quest.cinema_night.desc: They're showing a film at the Rassvet. The poster promises everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist.
quest.cinema_night.done: I came out of the cinema and the light outside had changed. For five minutes the town seemed like the film carrying on.
quest.cinema_night.film.log: A ticket is thirty roubles; the show runs while the projectionist is in, from three till late. I'll sit wherever I like.
quest.cinema_night.title: The evening show
quest.cinema_night.watch.obj: Watch a film at the Rassvet
quest.city_tour.desc: The town is big and I don't know anyone in it. I'll start by just walking through the main doors.
quest.city_tour.done: I've been round the whole centre. Every door greeted me as if I'd been there before.
quest.city_tour.see_cafe.obj: Go up to the Saucer café
quest.city_tour.see_club.obj: Look into the Rassvet culture house
quest.city_tour.title: The town by the sea
quest.city_tour.walk.log: The library, the department store, the market, the Rassvet, the clinic, the Saucer café. If I do something in each one, sit down, leaf through a book, buy something, maybe the town will remember me.
quest.first_chess.desc: At the Cog club there are people at the chess tables who never seem to get up.
quest.first_chess.done: After the game the buffet lady brought me tea "for bravery". She said losers always get a glass here.
quest.first_chess.game.log: I'll sit at a free board. Someone is bound to join me; that's the custom here.
quest.first_chess.play.obj: Play a game of chess at the Cog club
quest.first_chess.title: First game
quest.library_day.desc: The capsule library is quiet and smells of paper. You can sit there till closing and nobody will chase you out.
quest.library_day.done: My head is full of other people's pages. On my way out the librarian gave me a postcard: "So you have somewhere to write a thought down."
quest.library_day.read.log: I'll browse three shelves: birds, our town and the sun. There seem to be more books here about the sun than anything.
quest.library_day.title: A day at the library
quest.mineral_water.desc: The Druzhba sanatorium has a pump room. The guests go there on schedule, like going on a date.
quest.mineral_water.done: A taste of iron and of something warm. I drank it, and for a minute the sun seemed to shine from inside rather than out.
quest.mineral_water.drink.log: Now to drink it. Slowly, thinking of good things, as the sign says.
quest.mineral_water.fill.log: I'll fill a bottle at the tap by the entrance. They say the water comes out warm by itself, no heating at all.
quest.mineral_water.pump.obj: Fill a bottle of mineral water at the sanatorium
quest.mineral_water.title: Healing water
quest.photo_strip.booth.obj: Have my photo taken at the promenade studio
quest.photo_strip.desc: There isn't a single photo in my diary. Not even of me.
quest.photo_strip.done: I put the prints in my diary. The boy in them looks at me closely, as if he wants to ask something.
quest.photo_strip.photo.log: There's a photo studio on the promenade. Twenty roubles and I'll have proof I was here.
quest.photo_strip.title: A photo to remember
quest.school_lesson.board.log: The teacher said: "New boy, to the board!" Well then. To the board.
quest.school_lesson.desc: You can hear School No. 1's bell from the street. I wonder if anyone would notice if I quietly sat at the back.
quest.school_lesson.desk.obj: Sit through a lesson at the school
quest.school_lesson.done: Got a B for an answer I don't remember giving. The teacher said: "Come again, there'll always be a place for you here."
quest.school_lesson.lesson.log: Lessons run on weekdays from eight till three. I'll find a classroom and a free desk.
quest.school_lesson.title: The lesson
quest.store_errand.buy.log: The grocery counter on the ground floor has kefir and bread. I'll buy them while I'm here.
quest.store_errand.deliver.log: Now to the Stepped House, flat 4. I'll leave the bag at the door and sit on the bench outside for a bit, in case she looks out.
quest.store_errand.desc: A note on the department store door: "Anyone going to the Stepped House: please bring kefir and a loaf to flat 4. Money under the mat. Thank you!"
quest.store_errand.done: While I sat on the bench the bag by the door vanished. Under the mat: the money and a note: "You're a good person. Come round for tea." No signature.
quest.store_errand.stepped_house.obj: Take the shopping to the Stepped House and sit outside
quest.store_errand.title: A note on the door
